sections.overview: Neolamprologus brichardi is a small cichlid endemic to northern Lake Tanganyika in East Africa.
sections.identification: FishBase records a maximum total length of 9 centimetres.
sections.habitat: It lives in the northern part of Lake Tanganyika, a large rift lake shared by several East African countries.
sections.diet: FishBase classifies it as a plankton feeder; detailed species-specific diet measurements were not found in the sources consulted.
sections.behavior: Breeding pairs jointly defend their territory, and young helpers can take part in brood care and territory defense.
sections.reproduction: It lays eggs in a sheltered breeding site; parents and helpers tend the developing brood.
sections.ecology: Cooperative breeding is well studied in this fish, making it a notable example of social behavior among cichlids.
sections.conservation: FishBase reports a 2025 IUCN assessment of Least Concern; the species is also collected for the aquarium trade.
